transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello. I get this overwhelming, out-of-proportion fear whenever I even think about driving over certain bridges or high stretches of road. It has really started to take over my life, so my husband and pastor suggested I come talk to someone.

Do these intense fear episodes happen only when you’re on or thinking about bridges or high roads, or do they also come out of the blue in other situations? Are you mainly afraid of the bridge itself, or of having a panic-like episode and not being able to escape or get help there?

These intense feelings only happen when I'm facing, thinking about, or driving on bridges and high roads; they never just come out of the blue. My main fear is definitely about the bridge itself—specifically, this terrifying thought that my car is going to slide right off the edge, which has haunted me ever since I saw that bad accident.

Do you usually avoid bridges and high roads or endure them with intense fear, and has this been going on for at least 6 months? Has it been interfering with work, errands, or other parts of your life?

Yes, I avoid them by driving 20 minutes out of my way, and if I absolutely must cross one, I grip the wheel for dear life while my husband talks me through it. This has been going on for over two years now and has really shrunk my world. I've had to skip my quilting group, turn down food-pantry deliveries, and rely heavily on my husband to drive me places.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a circumscribed, marked fear triggered specifically by bridges and high roads, with immediate anxiety on exposure or anticipation, active avoidance, persistence for over 2 years, and clear functional impairment. The fear is focused on the specific situation itself rather than unexpected panic attacks or broader agoraphobic concerns, supporting specific phobia.
